decisions.why: The perfect of *stare* (ἔστη, aorist): God has taken his stand in the council, as a judge rises in court; the verb of the second colon (*dijúdicat*) is a present, and the Latin mixes the tenses. The glossary's *stare* row is *estar de pé*, and 37:12 put the perfect *stetérunt* as *ficaram de pé*. *Deus ficou de pé* is heard first as 'God remained standing' (as if the others sat); *Deus esteve de pé* is flat and seems to say he no longer is. *Se pôs de pé* says the act of the aorist and keeps the standing the Latin names. *Pôr-se* is *astáre*'s verb only with *diante de* / *à direita de* (glossary, 5:5); *pôr-se de pé* is the plain idiom for standing up and the *astáre* row itself lists it as the posture of *stare*. MS1932 *está presente* drops the posture; DRB 'hath stood'.

options.label: se pôs de pé
options.note: Ruling: the aorist's act, the posture kept.

options.label: ficou de pé
options.note: 37:12's form for the perfect; heard as 'remained standing'.

options.label: está de pé
options.note: the perfect read as a resultative present ('stands'); the Latin's tense lost.

options.label: está presente
options.note: MS1932; the posture lost.

decisions.why: The *synagóga* row (open) is *congregação* (7:7b, and 21:17 for *concílium* = συναγωγή); the cognate is a building. The row itself names *assembleia* as 'the right word for 81:1' — a council of gods sitting in judgement — but *assembleia* is *ecclésia*'s (D34), and taking it here would make a third Latin word share it. Held to the row so that the four places of *synagóga* (7:7b, 81:1, 85:14, 105:18) read alike; the risk the row records (heard as a religious community) is put to the ambiguity reader.

options.label: congregação
options.note: Ruling: the glossary row, one word for συναγωγή.

options.label: assembleia
options.note: the row's own option for this verse; clearer as a council, but *ecclésia*'s word (D34).

options.label: conselho
options.note: MS1932; *conselho* is *consílium*'s (D33).

decisions.why: Three small things. (1) *In médio* has no genitive; Portuguese *no meio* alone is left hanging, so *deles* is supplied (DRB 'in the midst of them', MS1932 *no meio deles*) — grammar, D2. (2) *Autem* is the light δέ, carried by *e*. (3) *Dijúdicat* is the only place of the compound in the psalter (grep; Isaiah 66:16 in a canticle besides): L&S gives 'judge, decide between', and with a person as object 'judge'. DRB and MS1932 both say *julga*. It stays *julgar*, so that the psalm's one root of judging (*dijúdicat, judicátis, judicáte, júdica*) sounds four times in Portuguese as in Latin; *faz juízo entre os deuses* keeps the *di-* and is the option. *deórum … deos* are the Latin's repetition: *deuses* stands at mediant and final, accepted. v2: the stylist heard the doubled *deuses* at mediant and final as a flat chime (checks flagged it too); his order ends on *deles*, a faint assonance, not the same word. The Latinist asked *porém* for *autem* (minor): refused — δέ here continues the scene (he stands in the council, and in its midst he judges), there is no contrast to mark, and *porém* in a short colon weighs more than the Latin particle; *e no meio, porém, julga os deuses* is kept as an option. *deles* stays: the Latinist called it harmless.

decisions.why: *Judicáre iniquitátem* (κρίνετε ἀδικίαν) is an internal accusative: 'judge unjustly', DRB and MS1932 both. Word for word, *julgais a iniquidade* is heard as 'you pass judgement on iniquity' — the opposite. *Com iniquidade* keeps the noun (the *iníquitas* row) and changes only the case, which D2 allows. The Latin's present is kept (*julgais*, ἕως πότε κρίνετε); MS1932 puts a future.

options.label: julgais com iniquidade
options.note: Ruling: the noun kept, the case turned.

options.label: julgais iniquidade
options.note: the accusative to the letter; heard as judging iniquity.

options.label: julgareis injustamente
options.note: MS1932; the noun lost, the tense moved.

decisions.why: πρόσωπα λαμβάνετε, 'take up / accept the faces', the Hebrew idiom for partiality (DRB 'accept the persons of the wicked'). Rule 5: the face stays. *Aceitar* is the plain verb that makes the idiom heard (to accept someone's face = to favour him); *tomar as faces* is heard as putting on their faces. The plural is the Latin's. *Fazer acepção de* is the Portuguese church idiom born of this very phrase, but it drops the face and needs a word few use; MS1932 paraphrases (*tereis respeitos humanos a favor dos pecadores*). v2: the stylist found the plural *faces* heard as cheeks and asked the singular (number is grammar, D2: *a face dos pecadores* is distributive, as in *a face da terra*). His verb *acolheis* is refused: the ambiguity reader already heard *aceitar* as 'welcome sinners', and *acolher* is the welcoming verb itself; it is kept as an option.

options.label: aceitais a face dos pecadores
options.note: Ruling (v2): the face kept, in the singular.

options.label: aceitais as faces dos pecadores
options.note: draft 1 — the image kept, the verb that carries the idiom.

options.label: tomais as faces dos pecadores
options.note: *súmere*'s plain verb; heard as taking on their faces.

options.label: fazeis acepção dos pecadores
options.note: the church idiom; the face lost.

options.label: acolheis a face dos pecadores
options.note: the stylist's verb; heard as hospitality.

decisions.why: The dative of advantage with *judicáre*, as 9:39 *judicáre pupíllo et húmili* → *julgar em favor do órfão e do humilde*: the same build, so the same words (rule 6). *Egénus → necessitado* (D38's row, 69:6), *pupíllus → órfão* (row). MS1932 *Fazei justiça ao necessitado* loses the psalm's verb of judging.

decisions.why: δικαιώσατε, forensic: declare the humble and poor in the right (DRB 'do justice to'). *Justificai* is heard as 'make excuses for' (72:13's reader, glossary *justificáre cor*). *Fazei justiça a* keeps the root *just-* and says the forensic act. The Latin's chiasm (verb–objects : objects–verb) is kept: *ao humilde e ao pobre fazei justiça* is natural Portuguese and ends on a paroxytone. *Dai razão a* is exact to the court sense but loses the root.

options.label: fazei justiça
options.note: Ruling: the root kept, the chiasm kept.

options.label: dai razão
options.note: the court's idiom; MS1932 *atendei à razão*; the root lost.

options.label: justificai
options.note: the cognate; heard as 'make excuses for'.

decisions.why: The *erípere* row: *libertar* where no source is named in the phrase, *arrancar* where *de …* follows. Here the colon names none — *de manu peccatóris* belongs to *liberáte* in the second colon, though the sense reaches back. *Libertai* is safe (past *libertei*) and stays apart from *livrai* (*liberáre*), as the Latin has two verbs. *Arrancai o pobre*, alone at the head of a verse, sounds violent. v2: the Latinist (minor) found *libertai … livrai* two near-synonyms where the Latin's verbs differ (*erípere* is to snatch away). The row gives *arrancar* where a source is named, and *da mão do pecador* is named in the same verse and is heard with both verbs (the Greek has ἐκ χειρὸς between them). Taken.

options.label: Arrancai
options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latinist's; the row's verb where a source is named in the verse.

options.label: Libertai
options.note: draft 1 — the row, no source in the colon.

options.label: Tirai
options.note: MS1932; *tirar* is *auferre*'s (D41).

decisions.why: Plural humans are *vós* (rule 3). The Latin names no pronoun here and names *Vos* in the next verse, where it turns the thought (*Vos autem*); *Sois deuses* keeps that shape. The verse is quoted in John 10:34 (Clementine *Ego dixi, dii estis* — not fetched; from the DO Latin only, the same words here). *Vós sois deuses* is the option.

options.label: Sois deuses

options.label: Vós sois deuses

decisions.why: *Excélsus* as a title of God (ὕψιστος; also 76:11 *déxteræ Excélsi*). The glossary keeps *excélsus → excelso* apart from *Altíssimus → Altíssimo* though the Greek is one (D43), so the title is *o Excelso*, as MS1932. The Ps 46 reader did not know *excelso* as an adjective; as a title after *filhos do* it is plainer. *Altíssimo* is the option, if Gustavo would rather the Greek decide.

options.label: Excelso
options.note: Ruling: the row (D43); MS1932.

options.label: Altíssimo
options.note: the Greek's ὕψιστος as *Altíssimus* elsewhere; merges two Latin words.

decisions.why: Both cola end on a future in *-eis* if the Latin's order is kept (*morrereis … caireis*): a rhyme at mediant and final that the Latin does not have (*moriémini / cadétis*). The first colon therefore puts the verb before *como homens*; the second keeps the Latin's verb-last (*e como um dos príncipes caireis*), which also avoids ending the verse on the proparoxytone *príncipes*. *Autem* is *Mas*, the turn against 81:6 (glossary *ego autem → mas eu*).

options.label: Mas vós morrereis como homens
options.note: Ruling: no rhyme with *caireis*.

options.label: Mas vós, como homens, morrereis
options.note: the Latin's order; rhymes *morrereis / caireis*.

options.label: Vós, porém, morrereis como homens
options.note: *autem* after the subject, as the Latin.

decisions.latin: quóniam tu hereditábis in ómnibus géntibus
decisions.why: κατακληρονομήσεις ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν; DRB 'thou shalt inherit among all the nations'. The Latin has *in*: God's inheritance is *among / in* the nations, not the nations themselves (which is the Hebrew's sense, and MS1932's *todas as nações são tua herança*). *Herdar em* is not Portuguese; *entre* is DRB's 'among'. *herdar* as in 24:13 and Ps 36 (*herdarão a terra*). *Tu* is named in the Latin, so *vós* is named. v2: the stylist found *herdar entre* odd and asked *em*, which is the Latin's preposition too; the ambiguity reader could not place *entre*. Taken. His cleft *porque sois vós que herdareis* is refused: it adds an emphasis construction for the plain *tu*, and *vós* already stands named; kept as an option.

options.label: em todas as nações
options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latin's *in*; the stylist's preposition.

options.label: entre todas as nações
options.note: draft 1 — DRB 'among'.

options.label: todas as nações
options.note: the nations as the inheritance — the Hebrew's sense (MS1932), not the Latin's; refused.

options.label: sois vós que herdareis em todas as nações
options.note: the stylist's cleft; an emphasis construction for the plain *tu*.

choices.81:1: v2: the stylist's order (*e julga os deuses no meio deles*) ends on *deles*; draft 1 had *deuses* at both cadences, the Latin's repetition (*deórum … deos*) put where the Latin does not put it.
choices.81:3: Both cola run long (+4, +3): the first is 9:39's build (*julgar em favor do órfão*), the second the forensic *fazer justiça a* for one Latin verb; each still one breath. Accepted.
choices.81:4: *liberáre → livrar* (row); the Latin's chiasm in this verse (*erípite páuperem : egénum … liberáte*) is not kept — verb-last in the second colon would read inverted; the chiasm of 81:3 is kept because there it reads naturally.
choices.81:5: *movéri → ser abalado* (row, 12:5b; one Greek σαλεύω). *Nescíre → não saber*, *intellégere → entender* (row), *ambuláre → andar* (row), present *andam* as the Latin. The second colon is three syllables over the Latin; accepted.
choices.81:6: *e sois todos filhos do Excelso* (v2, the stylist's): the copula of the first colon repeated, which D2 allows; draft 1's verbless *e todos filhos do Excelso* sounded clipped to him. *omnes* before *filhos* (MS1932's order). *Excelso* was listed as unknown by the ambiguity reader; kept under the row (decision `excelsi`).
choices.81:8: *Surge → Levantai-vos*, as *exsúrgere* (glossary; the Greek is ἀνάστα in both); 131:8 *Surge, Dómine* should follow. *Deus* bare in the vocative (row). *julgai* is safe (past *julguei*).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from the parallels (no Diurnal text for this psalm in the parallels file). Hard readings: 81:1 *stetit* (tense and posture) and *synagóga deórum*; 81:2 the internal accusative *judicátis iniquitátem* and the idiom *fácies … súmitis*; 81:3 the dative with *judicáre* (= 9:39) and forensic *justificáte*; 81:8 *hereditábis in*, which is not the Hebrew's 'inherit the nations'.

Hard pass. Soft: 81:1 rhyme *deuses / deuses* (the Latin's repetition; accepted); 81:3 +4/+3 (accepted, see choices); 81:5a −4, 81:7 −4/−3, 81:8b −3 (Portuguese shorter; accepted); 81:5b +3 (accepted).

Gate on draft 2 — claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. Clean of majors: one minor, 81:1 (*autem* as *e*, the supplied *deles*), held. Everything taken in v2 (*Arrancai*, *a face*, *e sois todos*, *em todas as nações*) passed; he named them Septuagintal idioms preserved.
